pumac-2022-finals-a-01.prompt:
Let $f:\mathbb Z_{>0}\to\mathbb Z_{>0}$ be a function which satisfies $k\mid f^k(x)-x$ for all $k,x\in\mathbb Z_{>0}$ and $f(x)-x\le2023$. If $f(1)=2000$, what can $f$ be?

*Remark:* Here, $f^k(x)$ denotes the $k$-fold application of $f$ to $x$.
pumac-2022-finals-a-01.answer: $f(x)=x+1999$ for every $x$ outside a set $F$ of fixed points, $f(x)=x$ on $F$, where $1\notin F$ and ($z\in F$, $z>1999\Rightarrow z-1999\in F$). In particular $f(x)=x+1999$ for all $x$ works, and it is the only choice with no fixed points.
pumac-2022-finals-a-01.reviewNote: The official PUMaC site gives no solution for the individual finals; the classification here was derived independently. The problem as printed also admits fixed points (any set F as described), so f(x)=x+1999 for all x is not the only solution.

pumac-2022-finals-a-03.prompt:
Let $n$ be a positive integer. We call a $n$-tuple $(a_1,\ldots,a_n)$ of positive integers *nice* if

- $\gcd(a_1,\ldots,a_n)=1$, and
- $a_i\mid a_{i-1}+a_{i+1}$, for all $i=1,\ldots,n$ (we define $a_0=a_n$ and $a_{n+1}=a_1$ here).

Find the maximal possible value of the sum $a_1+\cdots+a_n$ if $(a_1,\ldots,a_n)$ is a nice $n$-tuple.
pumac-2022-finals-a-03.reviewNote: The official PUMaC site gives no solution for the individual finals; the maximum and its proof were derived independently (brute force for n <= 6 agrees).
